evidence: tests/unit/test_reviewed_tree_binding_heldout_da31.py:126: monkeypatch only replaces `_resolve_reviewed_head`, which never touches `called`
ABSENCE: no `called.append(...)` sink is installed on any gate import (`produce_code_review_verdict`) or LLMConfig path, so the list is guaranteed empty regardless of ordering
`called: list[str] = []` (line 125) is never mutated — no monkeypatch wires produce_code_review_verdict or the gate imports to append to it
`assert called == []` (line 131) is therefore true regardless of whether review work executed before the raise
Docstring claims 'Proven by the absence of any gate import/call on the mismatch path' but no gate call is instrumented; only pytest.raises(ReviewedTreeMismatch) actually gates
adapter.py:297 `_assert_reviewed_tree(...)` precedes the gate try-block, so pytest.raises alone would still pass even if the ordering regressed
advisory.finding: test_binding_is_checked_before_any_review_work asserts `called == []` but nothing ever appends to `called` (no monkeypatch on the gate import / produce_code_review_verdict records a call), so the assertion is vacuously true and does not prove its stated claim that no review work precedes the binding check — it would still pass if the gate ran first.
merged_from: test_binding_is_checked_before_any_review_work asserts `called == []` against a list that nothing ever appends to; the assertion is vacuously true and does not verify the stated 'binding is checked before any review work' contract. The test would still pass if _assert_reviewed_tree were moved after the LLM gate call, so it is regression-blind for the very ordering it claims to prove.
scenarios: A future refactor that moves _assert_reviewed_tree after the gate import/run would not be caught by this test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch the gate seam (e.g. patch rebar.llm.workflow.gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict to `called.append`) before calling code_review_decision, so the empty-list assertion meaningfully proves no review work ran on the mismatch path.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 258 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug da31-f9d1-a81d-448c has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan da31-f9d1-a81d-448c` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review da31-f9d1-a81d-448c` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan da31-f9d1-a81d-448c --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
